meta.subtitle: AI optics demand has rebuilt the P&L; at $1,045.78 the price already discounts much of the consensus FY28 path

analystCommentary:
Lumentum has turned from a cyclical telecom-optics supplier into a capacity-constrained AI infrastructure name in two years. FY26 revenue rose {+83.2%+} to $3.01 billion and GAAP operating margin swung to 17.4% from -10.9% in FY25. Management guides the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion of revenue, and says demand is outpacing supply.

The operating story is not in dispute; the price is. At $1,045.78 the stock trades near the top of a 52-week range that starts at $147.81, at 31.1x trailing sales and 30.1x consensus FY28E EPS of $34.73. That multiple assumes consensus revenue of $9.7B in FY28 arrives on schedule.

The headline GAAP loss of $6.9 billion is a one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion loss on equitizing convertible notes, not an operating problem. Its real cost is dilution: diluted shares used in the Q4 calculation were 84.6 million against 72.0 million a year earlier.

We rate LITE HOLD with a $950–$1,250 target range. The bull case needs FY28E delivered and a premium multiple held; the bear case needs only a repeat of an inventory digestion like FY24, when revenue fell 23.1%.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Lumentum Holdings Inc. designs and manufactures optical and photonic products: semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems and wavelength management systems (Components), and optical modules, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers (Systems). Its products serve cloud, AI/ML, telecommunications, consumer and industrial markets.

During the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 the company reorganized and now reports as a single segment, managed by one team under CEO Michael Hurlston. It is headquartered in San Jose, California.

thesis.body: Demand for AI data center optics has lifted revenue, margins and cash generation at the same time, and the Q1 FY27 guide extends that run. We think the shares already price most of it: the stock sits near its 52-week high and the consensus target of $1,159.40 implies only +10.9%. Our probability-weighted value lands close to the current price, and the downside if AI spending pauses is large, so the reward/risk does not clear our BUY bar.

catalysts: Q1 FY27 delivery against the $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion revenue guide and the 39.5% to 40.5% non-GAAP operating margin guide.
Ramp of optical circuit switches and 1.6T cloud modules, which management calls key growth drivers that are beginning to layer in.
Early in-rack optics: ultra-high-power CPO lasers, an initial order for ELS modules and NPO engagements.
Capacity additions, internal and at contract manufacturers, that loosen the current supply allocation.
risks: An AI capex pause or customer inventory correction, the pattern that cut FY24 revenue.
Customer concentration: the 10-K lists reliance on a limited number of customers and the ability to sell to a significant customer among its risks.
Tariffs and trade restrictions, with China and Thailand named in the risk factors.
Further dilution from the remaining convertible notes, flagged in the risk factors alongside the 2032 Capped Call.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY26 revenue was $3.01 billion, up {+83.2%+} from $1.6 billion in FY25. GAAP gross margin rose to 41.7% from 28.0%, and GAAP operating margin reached 17.4% after three years of losses.

The fourth quarter carried the acceleration. Net revenue was $1.01 billion, against $808.4 million in Q3 and $480.7 million in Q4 FY25, a year-over-year rise of {+109.3%+} per the press release. The vendor quarterly series in the Facts block shows Q4'26 revenue growth of +51.2%; it disagrees with the release, and we use the release figure. Q4 GAAP gross margin was 47.4% (non-GAAP 50.4%) and GAAP operating margin 27.8% (non-GAAP 36.6%).

Both product types grew. FY26 Components revenue rose {+79.7%+} and Systems revenue rose {+90.7%+}.

GAAP net loss of $6.9 billion, or $92.96 per diluted share, comes from the one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion loss on debt extinguishment tied to equitizing convertible notes. On a non-GAAP basis FY26 net income was $782.3 million, or $8.67 per diluted share. The GAAP P/E of -11.2x is therefore not a usable valuation anchor.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and short-term investments reached $2.7 billion at fiscal year-end, an increase of $1.9 billion over the year but a decrease of $433.9 million from the end of Q3. Total debt was $3.2B and net debt $1.2B.

The current ratio fell to 1.68 from 4.37 in FY25 because the remaining convertible debt now sits in current liabilities. Total equity rose to $4.6B from $1.1B as notes converted into stock. Interest coverage of 24.1x leaves debt service comfortable.

Working capital is building with the ramp. Inventories and accounts receivable both rose over the year, which fits a supply-constrained ramp, but they are the first lines to strain if orders slow.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose to $0.8B in FY26 from $0.1B in FY25. Capital expenditure stepped up to -$451.3M as the company adds capacity, and free cash flow turned positive at $300.1M, a 10.0% FCF margin after two negative years.

Capex is the swing factor. Management says demand is outpacing supply, so spending is likely to stay elevated, and FCF margin will lag operating margin while capacity is built. No dividend is paid, and the company states it does not intend to pay one for the foreseeable future.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers LITE trades at 31.1x sales, and the GAAP P/E of -11.2x is distorted by the extinguishment loss. On forward numbers the stock is 48.0x NTM earnings and 30.1x FY28E EPS of $34.73.

The Street is constructive: 27 analysts, 23 Buy, 4 Hold and 0 Sell, with a consensus target of $1,159.40 and a median of $1,186.00 inside a range of $820.00–$1,400.00. Even the consensus implies only +10.9% from here.

The pack carries no peer multiples, so we do not benchmark against named competitors. We value LITE on whether FY27E revenue of $6.3B and FY28E revenue of $9.7B arrive, and on what multiple holds if they do.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: OCS, 1.6T modules and in-rack optics layer in on schedule, capacity keeps pace, and FY28E revenue of $9.7B and EPS of $34.73 are met. The market holds a premium growth multiple, taking the stock to the top of the Street range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: FY27E revenue of $6.3B and EPS of $21.78 are broadly delivered, but supply limits and a maturing cycle compress the multiple as earnings grow. The shares track earnings rather than re-rate.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Hyperscaler AI spending pauses or customers digest inventory, as in FY24 when revenue fell 23.1% and gross margin dropped to 18.5%. Estimates are cut and the multiple de-rates toward the lower half of the 52-week range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We put half the weight on Base at $1,100, a quarter on Bull at $1,400 and a quarter on Bear at $620. The probability-weighted value lands close to the current price, so the expected upside is small.

The asymmetry is the issue. Bull adds about a third to the price; Bear removes about two-fifths. The bear case is not exotic: this company's revenue fell 23.1% in FY24 when customers cut inventory, and the stock traded at $147.81 within the last year.

Our $950–$1,250 target range brackets Base. We would turn more constructive on a pullback that improves the reward/risk, or on evidence that FY28E is conservative.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Lumentum has reported as a single segment since a reorganization in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, but it discloses revenue by product type. Components (laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems and wavelength management systems) generated $2,005.6 million in FY26, up 79.7%, and Systems (optical modules, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers) generated $1,008.4 million, up 90.7%. In Q4 Components were 64.5% of net revenue and Systems 35.5%. Components are the building blocks behind AI data center links; cloud modules and optical circuit switches are the newer Systems lines.

moatFactors.name: Laser and photonics technology
moatFactors.body: The company describes itself as an industry-leading provider of optical and photonic products by revenue and market share, and its laser chips sit inside customers' data center links. Its own risk factors also cite rapid technology change and intense competition, so the lead has to be re-won each product generation.

moatFactors.name: Volume manufacturing at scale
moatFactors.body: Demand is outpacing supply and the company is allocating output, which signals capability that is hard to replicate quickly. Capacity is being added both internally and at contract manufacturers, so part of the advantage rests on partners.

moatFactors.name: Customer relationships
moatFactors.body: Management cites close relationships with market-leading customers built over many years. The same concentration appears in the risk factors as reliance on a limited number of customers and limited leverage in negotiations with large customers.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Technology and manufacturing know-how give Lumentum real advantages in a period of constrained supply, and margins show it. Those advantages are less durable once supply catches up: the company's own history shows gross margin falling to 18.5% in FY24 when demand turned. Durability depends on staying a generation ahead in lasers and modules while large customers retain bargaining power.

points: Near-term visibility is high. Management guides the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion of revenue and $4.05 to $4.35 of non-GAAP diluted EPS, and says the midpoint reaches its target model more than a quarter ahead of schedule.
The Street expects FY27E revenue of $6.3B, up about 110%, and FY28E revenue of $9.7B. Those estimates leave little room for a supply or demand stumble.
New product layers: management names OCS solutions and the cloud module business, including 1.6T adoption, as drivers that are beginning to layer in.

In-rack optics: increasing demand for ultra-high-power CPO lasers, an initial ELS module order and NPO engagements are, in the CEO's words, the first signs optics are penetrating in-rack connectivity.
Industrial lasers, 3D sensing and LiDAR remain smaller, longer-dated options that management expects to add to the market opportunity over time.

management.leadership: Michael Hurlston became president and CEO early in 2025, succeeding Alan Lowe, who had led the company since it became public; the October 2025 proxy describes this as the first CEO transition in the company's history. The Board gave Mr. Hurlston a mandate to move the company beyond its legacy telecom business toward data center infrastructure. FY26 results show that repositioning taking hold. Wajid Ali is executive vice president and chief financial officer per the same proxy.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital is going into capacity: capex of -$451.3M in FY26, with management investing internally and with contract manufacturers. No share repurchases are recorded for FY26, and the company does not pay a dividend.

The key capital decision of the year was equitizing convertible notes, which cut debt but raised the share count and produced the $7.8 billion non-cash loss. The remaining convertible notes and the 2032 Capped Call keep dilution on the risk list.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated October 2025, the board chair and CEO roles are separate, and the chair, Penelope A. Herscher, is an outside, independent director. The board determined eight directors independent under Nasdaq standards, has Audit, Compensation and Governance committees, and held 15 meetings in fiscal year 2025. The proxy reports no related-person transactions above its $120,000 threshold. These facts predate the FY26 10-K and may have changed.
management.insiderOwnership: As of August 29, 2025, per the proxy, all directors and executive officers as a group (14 persons) beneficially owned 307,933 shares, less than 1% of the common stock. Institutional holders of 5% or more included The Vanguard Group at 10.2%, FMR LLC at 9.8% and BlackRock Inc. at 8.8%. Insider alignment rests on equity compensation rather than large personal stakes; the share count has risen since the convertible notes were equitized.

idiosyncratic: Demand cyclicality: the company's own history shows customers building and then cutting inventory, which drove FY24 revenue down 23.1% and gross margin to 18.5%. An AI spending pause would hit a company now valued for uninterrupted growth.

Customer and supplier concentration: the 10-K names reliance on a limited number of suppliers and customers, limited leverage with large customers, and order cancellations or delays among its principal risks.
Execution on capacity: meeting guidance depends on the company and its contract manufacturers adding output on time, and capex of -$451.3M in FY26 shows the scale of the build.

Dilution: the risk factors cite dilution from the convertible notes and the hedging activity of the 2032 Capped Call counterparties. Equitization has already lifted the share count, and the current portion of debt keeps the issue live.
risks.systemic: Trade policy is the main external risk. The 10-K flags tariffs, export controls and trade restrictions, naming China and Thailand, and warns that tariffs may raise cost of goods sold and pressure gross margin if costs cannot be passed on. Broader macro and geopolitical conditions, including the conflicts listed in the risk factors, could slow customers' capital spending. At 31.1x trailing sales, the stock is also exposed to a market-wide de-rating of AI-linked equities, independent of company results.

body: HOLD, target range $950–$1,250. Lumentum is executing well: FY26 revenue rose 83.2%, operating margin turned positive at 17.4%, free cash flow reached $300.1M, and the Q1 FY27 guide points higher again.

The price already reflects much of that. The shares trade near the 52-week high at 30.1x FY28E EPS, and our probability-weighted value sits close to the current price while the Bear case at $620 is deep. We would revisit on a pullback, or if results show FY28E revenue of $9.7B is conservative.
